title: Gumley
html_source:
We learn that a night watchman named Gumley was a member of the Invincibles Gang that murdered the Chief Secretary and Under-Secretary on May 6, 1882 (22 years prior to Bloomsday) in Phoenix Park.

In Chapter 12 “Cylops” we learn that Gumley was sued by Reuben J. Dodd for not paying a debt but the Recorder hears his hard luck story and dismisses the case.

Shortly after 1:00 A.M. Stephen spots Gumley in a watchman’s sentry-box in Chapter 16 Eumaeus. He knows that he is a friend of his fathers but avoids his detection.

There was no chance that Stephen would be detected because Bloom sees that Gumley is asleep on the job.

A little later, a street noise wakes the dozing night watchman and we learn that in spite of once having a decent income, he is a “broken down” alcoholic and nearly broke. It appears that he has been given the watchman’s job out of charity.

Gumley is still asleep When Bloom and Stephen emerge from the cabman’s shelter and head for Bloom’s house. Bloom thinks that it is appropriate that the ex-revolutionary is asleep on the job and “guarding” stones.
